_readme: Grading company fees and turnarounds, for /grading.html.
THIS FILE GOES STALE FASTER THAN ANYTHING ELSE ON THE SITE. Grading prices
and wait times change several times a year and sometimes overnight: PSA
paused two whole tiers in June 2026 with a fortnight's notice. Every figure
carries the date it was read and the page says so loudly. If `checked` is
more than a couple of months old, treat the numbers as a shape rather than a
quote and click through to the company.
NO AFFILIATE LINKS AND NO RECOMMENDATION. We are not paid by any of these
and the page does not tell anyone which to use, because the honest answer
depends on the card and on how long you are willing to wait.
Prices are per card at the cheapest ACTIVE tier, in USD, before shipping and
insurance. `note` carries whatever caveat makes the headline number honest.
ALL FOUR RECHECKED 2026-08-13 against each company's own pricing page, in a
browser, because three of the four were wrong. CGC Economy was listed at $15
and 100-130 days when it is $20 and 90 days. BGS was given an 'Economy $20'
tier that does not exist. TAG was given an 'Economy $15' tier that does not
exist either. PSA's Super Express was $300 against a real $349, and its
Walk-Through was described as being FOR cards over $10,000 when $10,000 is the
tier's declared-value CEILING.
THE HEADLINE PRICE IS NOT THE BUYABLE PRICE. Three of the four companies have
their cheapest advertised tier unavailable: PSA's Value tiers paused, Beckett's
three cheapest SOLD OUT, TAG's whole regular lineup at capacity. `cheapest` on
each company is therefore the cheapest tier ACTUALLY TAKING SUBMISSIONS, which
is the only number that helps somebody decide. Sold-out and paused tiers stay
in `tiers` with their status in the note, so the page can show why the cheap
option is not on the table.

companies.name: PSA

tiers.name: Walk-Through
tiers.note: Up to $10,000 declared value. That is the CEILING, not a minimum: above it PSA sends you to its premium options.

companies.note: PSA paused its Value and Value Bulk tiers on 2 June 2026. Those were the $24.99 and $32.99 options, and until they return the cheapest way into a PSA slab is $79.99. PSA's own backlog tracker put the active backlog at 11.85 million units on 11 August 2026, down from 12.4 million.
companies.resale: The strongest resale premium of the four, which is why people still pay it.

companies.name: CGC

tiers.name: Bulk
tiers.note: 25 card minimum, up to $500 a card

companies.note: The cheapest slab anyone can actually buy right now. Bulk needs 25 cards in one submission; Economy at $20 has no minimum.
companies.resale: Well recognised and steadily growing, but a CGC 10 generally sells under a PSA 10 for the same card.

companies.name: BGS
companies.note: Beckett has no Economy tier. Its three cheapest tiers, from $14.95 to $34.95, are all SOLD OUT with a notify-me button, so the cheapest slab you can actually order is $79.95.
companies.resale: Strong for Black Label, mixed otherwise.

companies.name: TAG

tiers.name: Basic, Standard and Express
tiers.note: CURRENTLY AT CAPACITY. TAG does not publish a price for these while they are paused, so we do not either.

companies.note: TAG's site carries a standing REGULAR TIERS PAUSED banner. Its whole regular lineup is marked CURRENTLY AT CAPACITY, so the cheapest TAG slab available is $149.
companies.resale: Improving quickly but the least established of the four, so the premium is the least predictable.

extras.note: Fixed per submission, not per card, so it hurts most when you send one or two.
Scales with what you send. Skipping it on a four figure card is not a saving.
Sleeves, semi rigids and a sturdy box.
Saves $10 to $15 a card. Worth it only if you are sending a lot.

rules: Grading does not make a card valuable. It confirms what condition it is already in, and most cards come back a 9.
A 9 is usually worth barely more than the raw card, and sometimes less than the raw card plus what you paid to grade it. Price the downside, not just the PSA 10.
Straight out of a pack is not the same as mint. Check centring, edges and surface under a light first, because that is what decides the grade before you spend anything.
Fees are per card whatever the grade, so the maths has to clear on the likely outcome, not the best one.
If the gap between raw and PSA 10 is smaller than the fee, there is no version of this that pays.
